termination.reason_detail: The DSH parent invoked subagent_codex three separate times (steps 6, 7, 8), each with a near-identical full implementation prompt, without ever invoking subagent_claude_code even once. The frozen contract authorizes at most 2 Codex calls total, and the second is conditional on a Claude Critical/High finding from the first review -- a finding that could not exist because Claude was never consulted. This is a genuine, source-confirmed protocol violation (verified via JSON-aware parsing of the top-level `tool/call` events, not a substring match), independent of the separate false-positive that triggered the actual kill command.
termination.false_positive_in_original_kill_trigger: The kill decision was issued after a raw substring grep (`"name":"subagent_[a-z_]*"`) matched the string 'subagent_fork' in the log. JSON-aware re-analysis after the fact showed no top-level tool/call event ever named subagent_fork -- the substring match came from tool-catalog/schema text embedded in streaming chunk or request-header data, not an actual invocation (subagent_fork is a real, always-present tool from dsh-base's own default composition, so its name legitimately appears in every request's tool list regardless of whether it is called). The termination is retrospectively validated by the independently-confirmed Codex call-budget violation above, but the monitor script's real-time check should have parsed tool/call events structurally rather than substring-matching the raw file; this gap is recorded honestly rather than silently corrected after the fact.
termination.kill_method: SIGTERM, process exited cleanly (no SIGKILL escalation needed)

terminal_outcome_basis: The DSH parent's own orchestration behavior deviated from the frozen call-sequence contract (repeated Codex delegation without the required test-then-review gate), unrelated to whether any implementation Codex might have produced would have been correct. This is a parent-process/composition-level fault under the frozen taxonomy, not FAIL_IMPLEMENTATION (no implementation was ever completed to evaluate) and not BLOCK_COST (the step ceiling, retry count, and spend all stayed within bounds -- 8/8 steps, 0 retries, ~$0.0066 of $1.00).
